guardrails: Avoid hot-path allocations and every-frame work.
Do not force board layout or common-layer redraws from ordinary tap/regrow/automation updates.

Preserve viewport culling and dirty-tile overlays on large fields.
Defer saves during active layout, panning, or redraw work.

design: Unlock path: Touch branch after Two-Handed Technique.
Uses palm_press icon asset to avoid introducing a new asset dependency.
Mouse-only for now, intentionally avoiding mobile long-press/drag conflicts.
mechanic: If the skill is owned, holding left mouse button repeats touches on a cooldown.
Cooldown starts at 230ms and improves by 28ms per level, capped at 135ms minimum.
Dragging to a new tile nudges the next repeat forward by a 48ms grace without touching on every pointermove.
Stops on pointerup, pointerupoutside, panning, blocking overlays, placement mode, or if the pointer is no longer a left-mouse hold.
Skips repeat while board layout/rendering is busy or display-object pressure is critical.
Does not spam blocked feedback on regrowing tiles; it backs off for 320ms.
performance_notes: Idle path is only a boolean check before calling the persistent update.
Pointermove path only resolves a tile while Persistent Touch is active, owned, and the next touch is far enough away to benefit from drag grace.
The actual touch continues to reuse handleTileClicked, preserving combo, drops, crits, audio, and existing save behavior.
verification: Stress hold/drag on ?stress&perf&tiles=237: no warnings/errors, frameSpikes 0, maxFrameDeltaMs 7 after drag.
Controlled comparison: idle had 8 dirty tile views; held sweep had 34 dirty tile views with frameSpikes 0.
